bibl.title: Tonotopic Organization of the Superior Olivary Nucleus in the Chicken Auditory Brainstem

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the topographic organisation of frequency and of response types in the chicken superior olivary nucleus
span.quote: The goal of the current study is to analyze the topographic organization of 1) sound frequency and 2) physiologically identified cell types. Specifically, is the tonotopic organization of the brainstem auditory pathway preserved in the SON?

span.label: whether the tonotopic organisation of the auditory brainstem is preserved in an inhibitory long-range projection nucleus
span.quote: The goal of the current study is to analyze the topographic organization of 1) sound frequency and 2) physiologically identified cell types. Specifically, is the tonotopic organization of the brainstem auditory pathway preserved in the SON?

span.label: quantifies tonotopy in an inhibitory nucleus, shows it is less precise than in excitatory nuclei of the same species, and gives a predictive model from position to best frequency
span.quote: These analyses led to three main conclusions: 1) sound frequency is linearly arranged from dorsal (low frequencies) to ventral (high frequencies) in SON; 2) this tonotopic organization is less precise than the organization of the excitatory nuclei in the chicken auditory brainstem; and 3) neurons with different response patterns to pure tone stimuli are interspersed throughout the SON and show similar tonotopic organizations.

span.label: existence
span.quote: These analyses led to three main conclusions: 1) sound frequency is linearly arranged from dorsal (low frequencies) to ventral (high frequencies) in SON; 2) this tonotopic organization is less precise than the organization of the excitatory nuclei in the chicken auditory brainstem; and 3) neurons with different response patterns to pure tone stimuli are interspersed throughout the SON and show similar tonotopic organizations.

span.label: tonotopic organization of an inhibitory auditory brainstem nucleus
span.quote: We analyzed the topographic organization of response features of neurons in the SON of chickens.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: By using in vivo single- and multiple-unit recordings we classified the characteristic frequency (CF), frequency selectivity, threshold, and response patterns of SON neurons.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: SON response patterns are inherited from its nucleus angularis input, which is why sustained and onset types and diverse tuning shapes appear there
span.quote: Firing patterns of SON neurons to ipsilateral tones appear to be shaped primarily by the inputs from the NA, one of two main excitatory inputs to the SON.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the narrow hearing range of the chicken makes the frequency-to-place function linear rather than logarithmic
span.quote: This linear relationship, as opposed to a log relationship often observed in auditory centers, is probably a consequence of the limited frequency range of hearing in chickens

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: summation of individually subthreshold spike waveforms raises the apparent threshold of multiple-unit recordings
span.quote: This increase reflects multiple-unit recordings with neuronal waveforms that individually were not detected by using our threshold criterion, but summed to form detectable waveforms at higher sound intensities.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the broad, non-restricted SON to nucleus laminaris projection supplies the anatomical substrate by which inhibition laterally sharpens frequency tuning
span.quote: This projection pattern suggests an anatomical substrate for lateral sharpening of frequency tuning in NL neurons.

span.label: inhibitory neurons in this system sit in a discrete projection nucleus rather than among principal cells, which is what makes their organisation separable at all
span.quote: Inhibitory components of many neuronal circuits comprise interneurons residing alongside principal neurons ( Huang et al., 2007 ). Thus, independent evaluation of the organizing features of these circuit components is difficult. However, in the auditory brainstem, inhibitory neurons often reside in nuclei that project to one or more targets, thus providing opportunities to study sensory mapping in inhibitory long-range projection nuclei

span.label: recording sites are located by electrolytic lesions and electrode tracks, then normalised into a common 3D nucleus so cases can be combined
span.quote: To combine data from all 19 reconstructed SONs, locations of the recording sites were converted into normalized distances along three orthogonal axes in the SON (see Materials and Methods). These normalized coordinates allowed all recording sites to be mapped in a standardized SON.

span.label: PCA is run first because it was unknown whether the map was linear or nonlinear, single or multiple gradients
span.quote: Because the presence and arrangement (linear or nonlinear, single or multiple gradients) of the tonotopic organization in SON were unknown, we performed principal component analysis (PCA) on the combined dataset to determine the appropriate dimension(s) to observe the possible tonotopic organization. The first principal component accounted for 72% of the variance in the data

span.label: SON inhibition widens dynamic range and sharpens temporal coding for sound localisation
span.quote: Inhibition from the SON expands the dynamic range and sharpens temporal coding of auditory neurons to enable sound localization

span.label: Threshold comparisons between sustained and onset responders may not be valid because the spike-rate criterion may not be equally sensitive across response categories.
span.quote: Caution should be used when comparing thresholds between sustained and onset responders because the spike rate criterion used to determine response threshold (see Materials and Methods) may not be equally sensitive between categories of responders.

span.label: Binaural response properties of SON neurons were not assessed, so a possible contribution of the nucleus laminaris projection remains unexplored.
span.quote: Also, we did not assess the binaural response properties of SON neurons in this study, which could reveal a currently unexplored contribution from NL's projection to SON response properties.

span.label: In most animals only a limited region of the SON was sampled, which is why individual maps had to be combined into a standardized SON.
span.quote: However, in most subjects we sampled a limited region of the SON.

span.label: the map is explicitly less precise than in excitatory nuclei of the same species, by both error magnitude and r-squared
span.quote: Both the large error magnitude and the relatively low r 2 value suggest that the frequency map in the SON is not as precise as the tonotopic organization in other brainstem auditory nuclei in the same species

span.label: prediction error varies widely along the tonotopic axis rather than being uniform
span.quote: Comparing the predicted and measured CFs, we found that error magnitude (|CF predicted − CF measured |) varied widely at each position along the calculated tonotopic axis

span.label: the threshold criterion may not be equally sensitive across response categories, so between-category threshold comparisons are cautioned against
span.quote: Caution should be used when comparing thresholds between sustained and onset responders because the spike rate criterion used to determine response threshold (see Materials and Methods) may not be equally sensitive between categories of responders.

span.label: multi-unit thresholds run higher than single-unit thresholds because sub-threshold waveforms sum
span.quote: Thresholds of multiple-unit responses tended to be slightly higher than the thresholds of isolated neuronal responses ( P < 0.01; Fig. 3C ). This increase reflects multiple-unit recordings with neuronal waveforms that individually were not detected by using our threshold criterion, but summed to form detectable waveforms at higher sound intensities.

span.label: suppressed responders were too rare to analyse spatially
span.quote: Suppressed responders were encountered too infrequently to assess their spatial distribution.

span.label: in most animals only a limited region of the nucleus was sampled, which is why standardisation was needed
span.quote: To combine data from all 19 reconstructed SONs, locations of the recording sites were converted into normalized distances along three orthogonal axes in the SON (see Materials and Methods). These normalized coordinates allowed all recording sites to be mapped in a standardized SON.

span.label: within an isofrequency slice, position carried no information about CF at all
span.quote: Next, we examined the possibility that the relatively low r 2 values reflected particular regions of the SON that did not match the predicted frequency organization. To address this possibility, the standardized SON was sliced into five sections containing approximately the same number of recording sites using isofrequency planes (inset in Fig. 6F ). Sections were collapsed along the tonotopic axis into 2D, and MRA showed no significant relation between these 2D locations of recordings and CF ( P > 0.05 for MRA of all slices).

span.label: retinotopy as the template for what a sensory map is and why it matters
span.quote: Moreover, quantitative maps provide predictive tools to determine the optimal stimulus for a particular neuron based on its location in the tissue. Using this information investigators can 1) relate anatomical, biophysical, and pharmacological characteristics of a neuron to sensory processing based on stimulus selectivity ( Smith and Rubel, 1979 ; Kuba et al., 2005 ); and 2) compare the precision of processing across sensory areas or across species.

span.label: tonotopy is treated here as a MATTER OF DEGREE with a measured precision, not as present or absent - the paper's second conclusion is that this map is less precise than others in the same species
span.quote: Both the large error magnitude and the relatively low r 2 value suggest that the frequency map in the SON is not as precise as the tonotopic organization in other brainstem auditory nuclei in the same species

span.label: the map is operationalised as a multiple regression of characteristic frequency on normalised 3D position, reported as r-squared - the same operationalisation Muniak2014 used for mouse DCN
span.quote: A linear equation ( Eq. 1 ) best fit the combined dataset, finding a significant but not strong correlation (r 2 = 0.62, P < 0.01) between CF and location within the SON.

span.label: characteristic frequency is defined as the frequency with the lowest response threshold, and threshold itself as two SDs above spontaneous rate
span.quote: Characteristic frequency (CF) was defined as the frequency with the lowest response threshold.

span.label: onset versus sustained are response patterns classified from post-stimulus histograms at 20 dB above threshold, and the paper finds they are spatially interspersed rather than segregated
span.quote: These results suggest that onset and sustained types of neuronal responses are not distributed in separate regions or patterns, but instead are interspersed throughout SON

span.label: replicates → Coleman et al., 2011 (previous characterization of the chicken SON)
span.quote: These activity patterns, and the relative proportion of each response type are consistent with our previous characterization of the SON in chickens ( Coleman et al., 2011 ).

span.label: builds-on → Moiseff and Konishi, 1983; Lachica et al., 1994; Tabor et al., 2011
span.quote: Past studies in the owl ( Moiseff and Konishi, 1983 ) and chicken ( Lachica et al., 1994 ; Tabor et al., 2011 ) have suggested that stimulus frequency may be systematically represented in the SON.

span.label: extends → Rubel and Parks, 1975 (tonotopy of other chicken brainstem auditory nuclei)
span.quote: Both the large error magnitude and the relatively low r 2 value suggest that the frequency map in the SON is not as precise as the tonotopic organization in other brainstem auditory nuclei in the same species ( Rubel and Parks, 1975 ).

span.label: extends → the tonotopic organisation established for excitatory nuclei of the chicken auditory brainstem
span.quote: Both the large error magnitude and the relatively low r 2 value suggest that the frequency map in the SON is not as precise as the tonotopic organization in other brainstem auditory nuclei in the same species

span.label: confirms → earlier suggestions from owl and chicken that frequency is systematically represented in the SON
span.quote: These analyses led to three main conclusions: 1) sound frequency is linearly arranged from dorsal (low frequencies) to ventral (high frequencies) in SON; 2) this tonotopic organization is less precise than the organization of the excitatory nuclei in the chicken auditory brainstem; and 3) neurons with different response patterns to pure tone stimuli are interspersed throughout the SON and show similar tonotopic organizations.

span.label: supports → the group's own earlier characterisation of SON response types and their proportions
span.quote: Seventy-three percent of isolated neurons generated sustained responses, either primary-like ( Fig. 1A ) or pauser-like patterns ( Fig. 1B ), 25% of isolated neurons produced onset response patterns ( Fig. 1C ), and 2% suppressed activity in response to ipsilateral tones

span.label: contradicts → the expectation that physiologically distinct SON cell types occupy distinct territories
span.quote: These results suggest that onset and sustained types of neuronal responses are not distributed in separate regions or patterns, but instead are interspersed throughout SON

span.label: tonotopic —is-a→ topographic organization
span.quote: Moreover, quantitative maps provide predictive tools to determine the optimal stimulus for a particular neuron based on its location in the tissue. Using this information investigators can 1) relate anatomical, biophysical, and pharmacological characteristics of a neuron to sensory processing based on stimulus selectivity ( Smith and Rubel, 1979 ; Kuba et al., 2005 ); and 2) compare the precision of processing across sensory areas or across species.

span.label: characteristic frequency —operationalised-as→ response threshold
span.note: CF is DEFINED through threshold, and threshold is itself defined as two SDs above spontaneous rate - a two-step operational chain
span.quote: Characteristic frequency (CF) was defined as the frequency with the lowest response threshold.

span.label: onset —contrasted-with→ sustained
span.note: and they are spatially interspersed rather than segregated, which is the paper's third conclusion
span.quote: Finally, we assessed frequency selectivity of SON neurons by measuring Q10, which increases with selectivity and CF (r 2 = 0.50, P < 0.01). Sustained responders showed higher frequency selectivity, i.e., narrower tuning curves, than onset responders

span.label: tonotopic —operationalised-as→ principal component analysis
span.note: PCA first to find whether a single gradient exists at all; 72% on the first component
span.quote: Because the presence and arrangement (linear or nonlinear, single or multiple gradients) of the tonotopic organization in SON were unknown, we performed principal component analysis (PCA) on the combined dataset to determine the appropriate dimension(s) to observe the possible tonotopic organization. The first principal component accounted for 72% of the variance in the data

span.label: superior olivary nucleus —distinct-from→ nucleus laminaris
span.note: weak-ish: the quote gives SON's role rather than naming the contrast. kept low
span.quote: Inhibition from the SON expands the dynamic range and sharpens temporal coding of auditory neurons to enable sound localization

span.label: regression
span.quote: Multilinear regression analysis (MRA) with linear and log equations was used to examine the tonotopic organization of each case

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: Principle component analysis (PCA) and MRA were used to determine the major tonotopic axis across the standardized SON.

span.label: eigen-decomposition of the covariance matrix
span.quote: Third, we computed the eigenvectors and eigenvalues of the covariance matrix to determine the principal components.

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Statistical evaluations were made by using Student's t-test or r 2 correlation, and statistical significance was achieved when P < 0.05.

span.label: coefficient of determination
span.quote: the coefficient of determination (r 2 ) indicated that 85% of the variation in CF could be accounted for by the location of the recording within SON

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: All data are presented as mean ± SD.

span.label: multiple regression analysis of CF on 3D position
span.term: multiple regression analysis of CF on 3D position
span.quote: A linear equation ( Eq. 1 ) best fit the combined dataset, finding a significant but not strong correlation (r 2 = 0.62, P < 0.01) between CF and location within the SON.

span.label: principal component analysis
span.quote: Because the presence and arrangement (linear or nonlinear, single or multiple gradients) of the tonotopic organization in SON were unknown, we performed principal component analysis (PCA) on the combined dataset to determine the appropriate dimension(s) to observe the possible tonotopic organization. The first principal component accounted for 72% of the variance in the data

span.label: coefficient of determination
span.quote: In the case shown in Figure 5A , the coefficient of determination (r 2 ) indicated that 85% of the variation in CF could be accounted for by the location of the recording within SON.

span.label: error magnitude between predicted and measured CF
span.term: error magnitude between predicted and measured CF
span.quote: Comparing the predicted and measured CFs, we found that error magnitude (|CF predicted − CF measured |) varied widely at each position along the calculated tonotopic axis

span.label: In most reconstructed nuclei characteristic frequency ran along the dorsal-ventral axis, low frequencies dorsally and high frequencies ventrally.
span.quote: In 14 cases the CF was predominantly mapped along the dorsal-ventral axis of the SON; from lower CF in the dorsal SON to higher CF in the ventral SON

span.label: A linear rather than logarithmic function best described the frequency map in the large majority of individual cases.
span.quote: In 15 cases, including the two shown in Figure 5A and B , a linear relationship best predicted the tonotopic organization.

span.label: The first principal component of the combined dataset captured 72% of the variance and was oriented dorsoventrally, following the CF gradient.
span.quote: The first principal component accounted for 72% of the variance in the data

span.label: The SON frequency map is less precise than the tonotopic organisation of other auditory brainstem nuclei in the same species, as shown by large prediction errors and a low r2.
span.quote: Both the large error magnitude and the relatively low r 2 value suggest that the frequency map in the SON is not as precise as the tonotopic organization in other brainstem auditory nuclei in the same species

span.label: Within isofrequency slices the residual scatter in CF was not related to medial-lateral or anterior-posterior position, so the imprecision is not confined to a particular subregion.
span.quote: Sections were collapsed along the tonotopic axis into 2D, and MRA showed no significant relation between these 2D locations of recordings and CF

span.label: Neurons with onset and with sustained response patterns are intermingled throughout the nucleus rather than occupying separate territories.
span.quote: These results suggest that onset and sustained types of neuronal responses are not distributed in separate regions or patterns, but instead are interspersed throughout SON.

span.label: Each of the two response types carries its own complete and similarly arranged frequency map, so the SON processes at least two kinds of information in parallel.
span.quote: Each type forms a complete tonotopic representation, and these maps show similar spatial arrangements.

span.label: Sustained responders were more sharply tuned than onset responders.
span.quote: Sustained responders showed higher frequency selectivity, i.e., narrower tuning curves, than onset responders

span.label: characteristic frequency runs linearly from low dorsally to high ventrally in the SON
span.quote: In 14 cases the CF was predominantly mapped along the dorsal-ventral axis of the SON; from lower CF in the dorsal SON to higher CF in the ventral SON

span.label: a linear relation fitted 15 of 19 individual nuclei, a log relation two, and two showed none
span.quote: In 15 cases, including the two shown in Figure 5A and B , a linear relationship best predicted the tonotopic organization. In two cases a log equation better fit the data, and in two cases no relation was observed

span.label: in the best individual case, 85% of CF variation was accounted for by position
span.quote: In the case shown in Figure 5A , the coefficient of determination (r 2 ) indicated that 85% of the variation in CF could be accounted for by the location of the recording within SON.

span.label: across the standardised nucleus the fit was significant but not strong, r-squared 0.62
span.quote: A linear equation ( Eq. 1 ) best fit the combined dataset, finding a significant but not strong correlation (r 2 = 0.62, P < 0.01) between CF and location within the SON.

span.label: the first principal component accounted for 72% of the variance and ran dorsoventrally
span.quote: Because the presence and arrangement (linear or nonlinear, single or multiple gradients) of the tonotopic organization in SON were unknown, we performed principal component analysis (PCA) on the combined dataset to determine the appropriate dimension(s) to observe the possible tonotopic organization. The first principal component accounted for 72% of the variance in the data

span.label: the map is less precise than the tonotopy of excitatory brainstem nuclei in the same species
span.quote: Both the large error magnitude and the relatively low r 2 value suggest that the frequency map in the SON is not as precise as the tonotopic organization in other brainstem auditory nuclei in the same species

span.label: within isofrequency slices, position carried no information about CF
span.quote: Next, we examined the possibility that the relatively low r 2 values reflected particular regions of the SON that did not match the predicted frequency organization. To address this possibility, the standardized SON was sliced into five sections containing approximately the same number of recording sites using isofrequency planes (inset in Fig. 6F ). Sections were collapsed along the tonotopic axis into 2D, and MRA showed no significant relation between these 2D locations of recordings and CF ( P > 0.05 for MRA of all slices).

span.label: onset and sustained responders are interspersed throughout the nucleus and share the same tonotopic organisation
span.quote: Both neuronal types showed a dorsal (low CF) to ventral (high CF) tonotopic organization ( Fig. 8C , Table 1 ).

span.label: 73% of isolated neurons were sustained, 25% onset and 2% suppressed
span.quote: Seventy-three percent of isolated neurons generated sustained responses, either primary-like ( Fig. 1A ) or pauser-like patterns ( Fig. 1B ), 25% of isolated neurons produced onset response patterns ( Fig. 1C ), and 2% suppressed activity in response to ipsilateral tones

span.label: sustained responders are more frequency-selective than onset responders
span.quote: Finally, we assessed frequency selectivity of SON neurons by measuring Q10, which increases with selectivity and CF (r 2 = 0.50, P < 0.01). Sustained responders showed higher frequency selectivity, i.e., narrower tuning curves, than onset responders

span.label: characteristic frequency (CF)
span.quote: Characteristic frequency (CF) was defined as the frequency with the lowest response threshold.

span.label: response threshold
span.quote: Response threshold was defined as the intensity at which the spike rate (or rate of multiple-unit activity) during the stimulus time exceeded the average spontaneous rate by two SDs.

span.label: Q10 (frequency selectivity)
span.quote: Frequency tuning curves were assessed by analyzing Q10, defined as the CF divided by the response bandwidth 10 dB above threshold.

span.label: center of mass of recording sites
span.term: center of mass of recording sites
span.quote: The center of mass of recording sites was defined as the mean of their positions in 3D.

span.label: tonotopic map
span.quote: Similarly, in the auditory system, sound frequency encoded along the sensory epithelium gives rise to “tonotopic” maps throughout the central auditory pathways.

span.label: characteristic frequency
span.quote: Characteristic frequency (CF) was defined as the frequency with the lowest response threshold.

span.label: response threshold
span.quote: Response threshold was defined as the intensity at which the spike rate (or rate of multiple-unit activity) during the stimulus time exceeded the average spontaneous rate by two SDs.

span.label: characteristic frequency (CF) of the recorded unit
span.term: characteristic frequency (CF) of the recorded unit
span.quote: The data were best fit by the multilinear regression function: (1) CF = 0.01 + 0.32 / + 4.09 v − 0.55 a

span.label: normalized medial-lateral, dorsal-ventral and anterior-posterior coordinates of the recording site
span.term: normalized medial-lateral, dorsal-ventral and anterior-posterior coordinates of the recording site
span.quote: where CF is the characteristic frequency in kHz, / is the normalized medial-lateral coordinate (lateral edge is 1), v is the normalized dorsal-ventral coordinate axis (ventral edge is 1), and a is the normalized anterior-posterior coordinate (anterior edge is 1)

span.label: tone frequency and sound pressure level presented to the ipsilateral ear
span.term: tone frequency and sound pressure level presented to the ipsilateral ear
span.quote: A high-resolution frequency response function was derived by presenting a series of low (0.05–2 kHz), middle (1–4 kHz), or high (2–5 or 6 kHz) tone stimuli

span.label: frequency selectivity (Q10)
span.quote: Frequency tuning curves were assessed by analyzing Q10, defined as the CF divided by the response bandwidth 10 dB above threshold.

span.label: response threshold at CF
span.quote: Response threshold was defined as the intensity at which the spike rate (or rate of multiple-unit activity) during the stimulus time exceeded the average spontaneous rate by two SDs.

span.label: body temperature of the animal
span.quote: The bird's body temperature was maintained at 40°C throughout all procedures by using a heating pad.

span.label: characteristic frequency
span.quote: Characteristic frequency (CF) was defined as the frequency with the lowest response threshold.

span.label: normalised position along three orthogonal axes
span.term: normalised position along three orthogonal axes
span.quote: To combine data from all 19 reconstructed SONs, locations of the recording sites were converted into normalized distances along three orthogonal axes in the SON (see Materials and Methods). These normalized coordinates allowed all recording sites to be mapped in a standardized SON.

span.label: response pattern, onset or sustained
span.quote: Seventy-three percent of isolated neurons generated sustained responses, either primary-like ( Fig. 1A ) or pauser-like patterns ( Fig. 1B ), 25% of isolated neurons produced onset response patterns ( Fig. 1C ), and 2% suppressed activity in response to ipsilateral tones

span.label: 310 multiple-units and 349 isolated neurons; CF 90 to 5,000 Hz — size of the recorded sample and the range of characteristic frequencies encountered
span.quote: Among the 310 multiple-units and 349 isolated neurons recorded in the SON, CF ranged from 90 to 5,000 Hz

span.label: Seventy-three percent — proportion of isolated neurons with sustained (primary-like or pauser-like) responses, against 25% onset
span.quote: Seventy-three percent of isolated neurons generated sustained responses, either primary-like

span.label: 72% — variance in the combined location-plus-CF dataset captured by the first principal component
span.quote: The first principal component accounted for 72% of the variance in the data

span.label: r 2 = 0.62, P < 0.01 — strength of the linear relation between CF and 3D location in the standardized nucleus
span.quote: finding a significant but not strong correlation (r 2 = 0.62, P < 0.01) between CF and location within the SON

span.label: 85% — variation in CF explained by recording location in the best single case
span.quote: the coefficient of determination (r 2 ) indicated that 85% of the variation in CF could be accounted for by the location of the recording within SON

span.label: 60% — variability in the standardized dataset accounted for by the multilinear regression, taken as the precision of the map
span.quote: When the standardized SON was analyzed, the multilinear regression function accounted for 60% of the variability in the dataset, an indicator of the precision of this topographical map.

span.quote: The data were best fit by the multilinear regression function: (1) CF = 0.01 + 0.32 / + 4.09 v − 0.55 a

span.label: r-squared 0.62 for the standardised nucleus — how much CF variation position accounts for - directly comparable with Muniak2014's 0.87 for mouse DCN, since the operationalisation is the same

span.quote: Because the presence and arrangement (linear or nonlinear, single or multiple gradients) of the tonotopic organization in SON were unknown, we performed principal component analysis (PCA) on the combined dataset to determine the appropriate dimension(s) to observe the possible tonotopic organization. The first principal component accounted for 72% of the variance in the data

span.label: 310 multiple-units and 349 isolated neurons, CF from 90 to 5,000 Hz — the sample and its frequency span
span.quote: Among the 310 multiple-units and 349 isolated neurons recorded in the SON, CF ranged from 90 to 5,000 Hz

span.quote: Seventy-three percent of isolated neurons generated sustained responses, either primary-like ( Fig. 1A ) or pauser-like patterns ( Fig. 1B ), 25% of isolated neurons produced onset response patterns ( Fig. 1C ), and 2% suppressed activity in response to ipsilateral tones

span.label: 12 to 75 sites per animal across 19 nuclei — sampling density
span.quote: We recorded from 12 to 75 sites per animal, and across all cases neuronal responses from all regions of SON were sampled.

span.label: two SDs above spontaneous rate — the stipulated threshold criterion
span.quote: Response threshold was defined as the intensity at which the spike rate (or rate of multiple-unit activity) during the stimulus time exceeded the average spontaneous rate by two SDs.

span.label: two-thirds of peak voltage — the stipulated cut for counting multi-unit events
span.quote: For multiple-unit recordings, neuronal events were counted when the voltage trace exceeded two-thirds the peak voltage of the recording. We used event counts to calculate the rates of multiple-unit activity.
